Question 1
?

Find the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints (−w,7z) and (5w,−3z).

a
(−2w,−2z)
b
(−w,2z)
c
(−w,−z)
d
(2w,2z)
e
(2w,3z)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let (xm,ym) be the midpoint between (−w,7z)⏟(x1,y1) and (5w,−3z)⏟(x2,y2).

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

(xm,ym)=(x1+x22,y1+y22)=(−w+5w2,7z+(−3z)2)=(−w+5w2,7z−3z2)=(4w2,4z2)=(2w,2z).

q-216947.worked_solution:
The given points are ${{(a,b)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{1},\,{y}_{1})}$, ${{(-2,0)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{2},\,{y}_{2})}$ and ${{(1,1)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{m},\,{y}_{m})}.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}_{m},{y}_{m}) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\ (1,1) & =(\frac{a-2}{2},\frac{b+0}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding $x$- and $y$-coordinates in the equation above gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}1=\frac{a-2}{2} \\ 1=\frac{b}{2}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}a=4 \\ b=2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $a=4$ and $b=2.$
